## Declarations and implementations

```plato
//==
// # IField expression graph evaluation
//
// Recursive evaluation of the flat expression graphs declared in
// `fields.types.plato`. Lives in its own `library` block, rather than in the
// interface-package libraries, because a graph walk needs a recursive dispatch
// over the node sum that an expression-only package file cannot host cleanly.
//
// Operands always reference lower-indexed nodes, so the recursion is well
// founded and terminates on any graph obeying that invariant. Source nodes
// resolve against a caller-supplied list of fields, which is what keeps the
// graph itself a plain value.

library FieldsGraphs
{
    // The value one planar node produces, given the graph it belongs to and the
    // external field list its Source nodes index into.
    EvalNode(node: ScalarFieldNode2D, graph: ScalarFieldGraph2D, sources: Array<ScalarFunctionField2D>, point: Point2D): Number =>
        match (node) {
            Source(fieldIndex) => sources[fieldIndex.Value].Eval(point);
            Constant(value) => value;
            Add(left, right) => graph.EvalNodeAt(left, sources, point) + graph.EvalNodeAt(right, sources, point);
            Subtract(left, right) => graph.EvalNodeAt(left, sources, point) - graph.EvalNodeAt(right, sources, point);
            Multiply(left, right) => graph.EvalNodeAt(left, sources, point) * graph.EvalNodeAt(right, sources, point);
            Divide(left, right) => graph.EvalNodeAt(left, sources, point) / graph.EvalNodeAt(right, sources, point);
            Minimum(left, right) => graph.EvalNodeAt(left, sources, point).Min(graph.EvalNodeAt(right, sources, point));
            Maximum(left, right) => graph.EvalNodeAt(left, sources, point).Max(graph.EvalNodeAt(right, sources, point));
            Negate(input) => graph.EvalNodeAt(input, sources, point).Negative;
            AbsoluteValue(input) => graph.EvalNodeAt(input, sources, point).Abs;
            Lerp(a, b, weight) => graph.EvalNodeAt(a, sources, point).Lerp(
                graph.EvalNodeAt(b, sources, point),
                graph.EvalNodeAt(weight, sources, point));
            Clamp(input, low, high) => graph.EvalNodeAt(input, sources, point).Clamp(
                graph.EvalNodeAt(low, sources, point),
                graph.EvalNodeAt(high, sources, point));
            Remap(input, fromLow, fromHigh) =>
                (graph.EvalNodeAt(input, sources, point) - graph.EvalNodeAt(fromLow, sources, point))
                / (graph.EvalNodeAt(fromHigh, sources, point) - graph.EvalNodeAt(fromLow, sources, point));
            Threshold(input, level) =>
                graph.EvalNodeAt(input, sources, point) >= graph.EvalNodeAt(level, sources, point) ? 1.0 : 0.0;
        };

    // The value the node at the given index produces.
    EvalNodeAt(graph: ScalarFieldGraph2D, index: FieldNodeIndex, sources: Array<ScalarFunctionField2D>, point: Point2D): Number
        => graph.Nodes[index.Value].EvalNode(graph, sources, point);

    // The graph's value at a point: the value its root node produces.
    Eval(graph: ScalarFieldGraph2D, sources: Array<ScalarFunctionField2D>, point: Point2D): Number
        => graph.EvalNodeAt(graph.Root, sources, point);

    // The value one spatial node produces; mirrors the planar walk.
    EvalNode(node: ScalarFieldNode3D, graph: ScalarFieldGraph3D, sources: Array<ScalarFunctionField3D>, point: Point3D): Number =>
        match (node) {
            Source(fieldIndex) => sources[fieldIndex.Value].Eval(point);
            Constant(value) => value;
            Add(left, right) => graph.EvalNodeAt(left, sources, point) + graph.EvalNodeAt(right, sources, point);
            Subtract(left, right) => graph.EvalNodeAt(left, sources, point) - graph.EvalNodeAt(right, sources, point);
            Multiply(left, right) => graph.EvalNodeAt(left, sources, point) * graph.EvalNodeAt(right, sources, point);
            Divide(left, right) => graph.EvalNodeAt(left, sources, point) / graph.EvalNodeAt(right, sources, point);
            Minimum(left, right) => graph.EvalNodeAt(left, sources, point).Min(graph.EvalNodeAt(right, sources, point));
            Maximum(left, right) => graph.EvalNodeAt(left, sources, point).Max(graph.EvalNodeAt(right, sources, point));
            Negate(input) => graph.EvalNodeAt(input, sources, point).Negative;
            AbsoluteValue(input) => graph.EvalNodeAt(input, sources, point).Abs;
            Lerp(a, b, weight) => graph.EvalNodeAt(a, sources, point).Lerp(
                graph.EvalNodeAt(b, sources, point),
                graph.EvalNodeAt(weight, sources, point));
            Clamp(input, low, high) => graph.EvalNodeAt(input, sources, point).Clamp(
                graph.EvalNodeAt(low, sources, point),
                graph.EvalNodeAt(high, sources, point));
            Remap(input, fromLow, fromHigh) =>
                (graph.EvalNodeAt(input, sources, point) - graph.EvalNodeAt(fromLow, sources, point))
                / (graph.EvalNodeAt(fromHigh, sources, point) - graph.EvalNodeAt(fromLow, sources, point));
            Threshold(input, level) =>
                graph.EvalNodeAt(input, sources, point) >= graph.EvalNodeAt(level, sources, point) ? 1.0 : 0.0;
        };

    // The value the node at the given index produces.
    EvalNodeAt(graph: ScalarFieldGraph3D, index: FieldNodeIndex, sources: Array<ScalarFunctionField3D>, point: Point3D): Number
        => graph.Nodes[index.Value].EvalNode(graph, sources, point);

    // The graph's value at a point: the value its root node produces.
    Eval(graph: ScalarFieldGraph3D, sources: Array<ScalarFunctionField3D>, point: Point3D): Number
        => graph.EvalNodeAt(graph.Root, sources, point);
}
```
